newsitem.title: GREECE: Natl Securities says Greek stocks not yet peaked.
newsitem.headline: Natl Securities says Greek stocks not yet peaked.

text.p: Athens stock exchange member firm National Securities said that despite their recent rally Greek equities had not yet peaked with improved confidence supporting expectations for a further advance.
"Despite the recent market rally, we still believe that we are not near a peak in the medium term," said analyst George Karousos in a market report.

It was a rebuttal to a Merrill Lynch report that Greek shares had an unattractive risk-reward profile at current valuations and could give up one third of the gains attained since the beginning of the year.

"The attractive market valuation coupled with political stability and improving macroeconomic performance have improved confidence, giving rise to expectations for further gains," National Securities said.

It cited end-January IBES consensus earnings per share (EPS) forecasts that showed the Athens bourse was trading at a multiple of 8.3 times 1996 earnings and 6.9 times 1997 expected earnings, implying a 1997/96 earnings growth rate of 20.3 percent.
"Based on these numbers international organisations like the IFC have ranked Greek equities among the cheapest in the emerging markets group," Karousos said.
But on Friday, Greek shares opened weak, continuing to give up recent gains. They were down 0.89 percent in early trade with the benchmark share index at 1,219.32.

In a report that stirred discussion, Merrill Lynch analyst Mike Harris saw limited potential for a further upside. He said Greek equities fall firmly in the sell territory of European emerging markets when weighing forecast P/E levels versus estimated earnings per share growth.
The Athens bourse has climbed 31.2 percent since the start of the year, with the index hitting 1,252.37 points on Wednesday, a level it hadn't visited in years.
